question: An 8-year-old child is brought to the emergency department because of profuse diarrhea and vomiting that have lasted for 2 days. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery. He is up to date on all vaccines and is meeting all developmental milestones. Past medical history is noncontributory. The family recently made a trip to India to visit relatives. Today, his heart rate is 100/min, respiratory rate is 22/min, blood pressure is 105/65 mm Hg, and temperature is 37.2ºC (99.0°F). On physical examination, he appears unwell with poor skin turgor and dry oral mucosa. His heart has a regular rate and rhythm and his lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally. His abdomen is sensitive to shallow and deep palpation. A gross examination of the stool reveals a ‘rice water’ appearance. Diagnostic microbiology results are pending. Which of the following is the best screening test to aid the diagnosis of this patient?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Profuse diarrhea and vomiting for 2 days" -> "Recent trip to India" -> "Rice water appearance in stool" -> "Cholera infection suspected" -> 80% confidence. CHAIN: "Profuse diarrhea and vomiting for 2 days" -> "Poor skin turgor and dry oral mucosa" -> "Dehydration" -> "Cholera infection suspected" -> 75% confidence. CHAIN: "Profuse diarrhea and vomiting for 2 days" -> "Sensitive abdomen to palpation" -> "Cholera infection suspected" -> 80%
analysis: Given the clinical presentation of profuse diarrhea and vomiting with a recent trip to India, along with the 'rice water' appearance of the stool, the most likely diagnosis is cholera. The best screening test to aid in the diagnosis of cholera is the string test.
